stem.en: Why is it harder to enforce rules on the high seas than in a territorial sea?

text.en: No rules of any kind reach the high seas.

feedback.en: Rules do exist on the high seas, including the laws of the flag state.

text.en: Ships on the high seas need no registration.

feedback.en: Every ship has a flag state, the country in which it is registered.

text.en: No single country controls those waters.

feedback.en: Yes. The high seas belong to no single country, so there is no one country to enforce the rules.

text.en: Only warships may sail on the high seas.

feedback.en: All countries have equal rights of navigation there, for every kind of ship.

explanation.en: In its territorial sea a country has near-complete control. The high seas belong to no single country, so ensuring safety and enforcing rules is more difficult, even though rules do exist.

hints.en: Compare who is in control in each place.
